answer: Each identity's usable standing is released only after a sequential, non-transferable custody period, and the release rate is super-linear in how many identities an operator runs, so a fleet cannot mature faster than one identity at a time. The cost of one more head is paid in full and is never amortised across the fleet. The pigment is the serial tenure, the sparrow the custody window that must elapse, and the dune the standing released at the end of it; the pigment is personal, the sparrow is not skippable, and the dune cannot be inherited by a sibling.
